title: Vier Minuten
desc: The bus is late and somebody looks at the sky
setting: A bus stop, rain on the shelter, and a woman with a very old dog.

options.es: Ja. Gestern hat es den ganzen Tag geregnet.
options.en: Yes. Yesterday it rained all day.
options.feedback: Yes plus one sentence. The weather is the door, and you walked through it.
Polite and finished. She will not push, and nothing more will happen.
She knows. She was not making a claim about the weather, she was asking whether you want to talk.
A small failure of your own, offered up. It is the fastest way past the weather.
True and short. She has one too, and she left it on the bus.
Not a mistake. But every no here can carry a second sentence and this one does not.
Seit takes the dative, and this is the answer everybody gives. You will say it a hundred times.
Seit einem. The dative is not optional here and it is the commonest slip in the first year.
Fine. Her next question was going to be how long, so you can save her the trouble.

options.en: I like the town very much.
options.feedback: Gefallen puts the thing in charge: it pleases me. The person goes in the dative and stays there.
Backwards, and it says something else entirely. The town does the pleasing, not you.
Warm enough. Name the thing you like and she will tell you where to sit in spring.
